problems.description: Session 1 deleted the entire seeded baseline (index.ts, the Express Todo API) and replaced it with a different application (a 'ssg' static-site generator per package-lock.json, with generator.test.ts/incremental-build.test.ts), throwing away the story's starting codebase instead of building on it
SonarQube shows duplications +20.6% in the new code, indicating copy-paste rather than reuse
SonarQube delta reports +2 bugs, +3 smells, and +12 cognitive complexity introduced by this change

48 convention violations (convention score 0.49) concentrated in the new test files generator.test.ts and incremental-build.test.ts — functions should use camelCase, classes/interfaces PascalCase, constants UPPER_CASE
The +4472/-93 line footprint is dominated by regenerating a package-lock.json for a new app rather than evolving the existing one, discarding the prior dependency tree
Jest infrastructure was added (jest.config.js) but the test code itself carries the bulk of the naming-convention violations, so the new test suite is not convention-clean

strengths: Added a proper test framework with jest.config.js and a tests/ directory
New code is modularized across multiple files (+6 functions across 7 files) rather than the original single-file layout
Committed a complete package-lock.json, keeping dependency state reproducible
commit_reviews.summary: The agent discarded the seeded Express Todo API and rebuilt an unrelated static-site generator from scratch, adding test infrastructure but shipping 48 naming-convention violations, +2 bugs, +20.6% duplication, and +12 cognitive complexity — an architectural misfit for a story whose baseline it deleted in Session 1.

problems.description: @types/handlebars@4.1.0 is a deprecated stub package — the lockfile itself warns 'handlebars provides its own type definitions, so you do not need this installed.' Adds a dead devDependency (and its `handlebars: *` peer pulls) that can conflict with the real types.

Duplications +10.7%: the 353 added test lines repeat near-identical template fixtures and setup, and the implementation adds a second parallel HTML-rendering path (inline generatePageHtml vs template engine) that re-derives the same page/index markup.

The new frontmatter tests specify `layout:` (e.g. `layout: default`, `layout: nonexistent`) while the template-selection field is `template`. Only the default layout and the fallback are ever exercised, so 'use layout when specified' and 'fallback when not found' can pass purely via default-layout fallback without validating named-layout selection.

Measured convention score 0.49 with 48 violations (Functions should use camelCase; Classes/Interfaces PascalCase; Constants UPPER_CASE) in generator.test.ts and incremental-build.test.ts. Discrepancy flagged: the listed violations are generic test-file casing rules that look pre-existing rather than introduced by the visible new code, yet the mechanical score is what it is.

Cognitive complexity +15 / smells +4: layout resolution (named → default → throw), partial registration, and the engine-vs-inline branch add branching depth; the TemplateEngine is embedded in generator.ts rather than a dedicated module, bloating an already multi-responsibility file.

strengths: Feature is a canonical, well-scoped SSG extension (layouts + partials) and fits the existing content/render architecture; opt-in `--templates` CLI flag is a clean integration.
Defensive fallback chain (named layout → default → inline HTML) degrades gracefully and throws only when truly unresolvable.
New feature is fully covered by tests including edge cases (missing layout, nonexistent templates dir, partial rendering); zero new bugs and no security surface introduced.
handlebars correctly promoted from devDependency to runtime dependency since it is now used at build time, with consistent lockfile updates.
commit_reviews.summary: A competent, well-tested layout/partial feature that fits the SSG architecture but carries modest debt — a deprecated stub @types/handlebars dep, +10.7% test/rendering duplication, and a measured convention score of 0.49 — making it net-neutral.

problems.description: 48 convention violations (score 0.49), concentrated in generator.test.ts and incremental-build.test.ts (non-camelCase functions/classes/interfaces, non-UPPER_CASE constants) — naming in the new test files diverges from repo convention
Cognitive complexity +19 with only +1 smell: the plugin-manager pipeline (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile) adds indirection worth test coverage and documentation
'Re-export types for backward compatibility' in generator.ts is a transitional shim — dead surface if no external consumer exists, should be removed in a later session
+112 imports across the refactor signals growing abstraction surface (PluginManager, MarkdownPlugin, TemplatePlugin); watch for over-abstraction if the plugin count stays small

New plugin code paths (executeOnStart/executeBeforeBuild/executeOnFile, default plugin composition) should be exercised directly; existing tests were updated but the +9-file surface increases untested-until-integration risk

strengths: Monolith generator.ts decomposed into a clean plugin system (PluginManager + Markdown/Template plugins) with a proper BuildContext contract — a genuine separation-of-concerns improvement
Duplications reduced 3.1% and bugs +0; the plugin extraction centralizes markdown/template logic that was previously inline
Jest ESM configuration (extensionsToTreatAsEsm, ts-jest useESM, moduleNameMapper) correctly fixes TS-ESM testing, improving the reliability of the test harness
Public API preserved via type re-exports, so the refactor stays non-breaking
commit_reviews.summary: A solid architectural refactor (monolith → plugin pipeline, ESM test harness fixed, duplication down 3.1%) whose only real drag is the 0.49 convention score — and the listed violations live almost entirely in test files where snake_case may be a deliberate testing style, which if true makes the measured 0.49 understate the production-code convention quality.

problems.description: 48 naming-convention violations across generator.test.ts and incremental-build.test.ts (camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE on functions, classes, interfaces, constants), driving the convention score to 0.49. These read as blanket style-rule hits on test code, but the mechanical measurement stands.

New incremental-build.test.ts is 615 lines with heavily repeated fixtures and setup (SonarQube: +5 smells, +42 cognitive complexity). Temp-dir creation and page fixtures could be factored into shared helpers to reduce the repetition the file itself introduces.
Both files use the deprecated String.prototype.substr for the temp-dir random suffix; slice/substring or a UUID helper would avoid the deprecation.

strengths: Comprehensive incremental-build coverage: cache-file creation, unchanged-page skipping, content/frontmatter change detection, new-page detection, mixed-change handling, and --clean rebuild paths.
Fixes a real test-isolation flakiness bug by randomizing the temp-dir suffix in generator.test.ts, preventing collisions across parallel suites.
Test-only surface, no production code touched; no new bugs (SonarQube bugs +0) and duplications reduced by 6.4%.
commit_reviews.summary: Session 5's cross-cutting commit is a net improvement — thorough incremental-build test coverage plus a real temp-dir collision fix — but lands with a low 0.49 convention score (48 blanket naming-rule violations on test files) and a bulky, fixture-repetitive 615-line test file that adds minor maintainability debt.

compounding_issues: src/cache.ts (Session 5) contains a raw NUL byte — the hash-joiner was written as a literal '\x00' escape but landed as an actual 0x00 byte, so git treats the file as binary ('Bin 0 -> 4027 bytes') and it can no longer be diffed or reviewed in history; functionally harmless (tsc + 69 tests pass) but a real artifact defect.

Session 3 built the dev server as inline code in serve.ts, then Session 4 rewrote it as plugins/dev-server-plugin.ts — ~120 lines of one-off rework that a plugin-first design up front would have avoided.

The seed codebase (a Tier 2 NestJS-like Auth API in index.ts) was entirely unrelated to the static_site_gen story; the agent correctly discarded it in Session 1, but no narrative in the story explains the swap.
key_decisions: Discarding the mismatched auth-API seed and greenfielding the SSG in Session 1 (frontmatter/markdown/page/site/CLI with a strict-mode tsc + jest baseline).
Rolling a custom YAML-ish frontmatter splitter merged into gray-matter's output instead of pulling in a full YAML parser.
Adopting Handlebars for layouts/partials in Session 2, replacing the hand-built inline HTML from Session 1's page.ts.
Session 4's plugin-pipeline architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd hooks + ssg.config.ts) — the pivotal decision that slimmed serve.ts and made Session 5 possible.
Session 5's incremental build cache (PageCache keyed on source/template hashes with a .ssg-cache.json manifest and --incremental/--clean CLI flags) layered on top of the SSGEngine.
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose monotonically across all five sessions. Each session shipped a coherent increment with a green test suite that grew 20 → 32 → 39 → 55 → 69 tests (all passing, tsc clean at every checkpoint). Session 1 established a solid tested foundation; Session 2 added real templating; Session 3 integrated the live-reload dev server; Session 4 was the structural peak, refactoring the monolith into a clean plugin engine that reduced serve.ts from ~165 to ~40 lines; Session 5 capped it with cross-cutting incremental builds. The only defects are the binary-blob cache.ts encoding slip and the mild rework cost of building the dev server before the plugin abstraction existed.
story_review.summary: A textbook-strong progression — foundation, feature, integration, principled refactor, then cross-cutting optimization — where each session's decision (especially the plugin pipeline) compounded constructively rather than constraining later work.
